tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Panel Line Tool
tips.text: For crisp panel lines, use RB Productions panel line tool. First, lightly scribe with the 0.3mm tool on raised details, then deepen with the 0.5mm tool on recessed areas. Apply gentle pressure, moving the tool along the line in one smooth motion. Use a sharp blade (X-Acto #11) for best results. After scribing, lightly sand with 5000 grit paper to remove burrs.

tips.title: Bending Photo-Etch with Eduard Bending Jigs
tips.text: Eduard bending jigs allow precise bending of photo-etch parts. Soak the part in warm water for 30 seconds, then bend it over the jig. For tight bends, use the narrow jig (0.3mm). For wider bends, use the medium jig (0.5mm). Apply even pressure, avoiding over-bending. After bending, dry the part immediately with a hairdryer on low heat.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Airbrush Cleaner
tips.text: Regular cleaning maintains airbrush performance. After each use, disassemble the needle and nozzle. Soak them in Iwata Airbrush Cleaner for 15 minutes, then scrub with a toothbrush. Rinse with water and dry thoroughly. Once a month, soak the parts in acetone to dissolve any dried paint residue. Always reassemble the needle with the flat side facing the front.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya and Kabuki Tapes
tips.text: For complex masking, use Tamiya tape for straight edges and Kabuki tape for curves. Tamiya tape is easier to apply but leaves more residue. Kabuki tape is more expensive but provides better adhesion and easier removal. For hard-to-reach areas, use Tamiya's masking stick (74522). Apply tapes with firm, even pressure, and remove them carefully after painting.

tips.title: Sanding Sticks Progression with ICM Sanding Sticks
tips.text: ICM sanding sticks allow controlled sanding of model surfaces. Start with 320 grit for heavy stock removal, then 400 grit for smoothing, and finish with 800 grit for a smooth surface. Wet sand using lubricant (ICM Sanding Liquid) to prevent clogging. Sand in linear motions, working diagonally to avoid damaging the surface. After sanding, wipe off residue with a damp cloth.
